title: Music-guided gait training for patients with parkinson's disease
summary: It is being investigated if a positive effect on the gait ability exists with the use of sensor based music feedback compared to music-guided training in the domestic self-training.

interventions.name: Seven times a week, 20 minute self-training with sensorbased music-feedback for three weeks.
Seven times a week, 20 minute self-training with music-supported gait training for three weeks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(1) Diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson Disease with the UK Brain Bank Criteria 
(2) Hoehn & Yahr-Stadium ≤ 4 (with medicinal On-State)
(3) Ability to complete the Gait tests without any aid and without fatigue
(4) Clinical manifested unilateral reduction in armswing with range of motion < 28,3° or marked reduction in gait velocity < 1,15 m/s measured in the 1-minute gait test
(5) No adaption of dopaminergic medication since one week and planned for eight weeks
Exclusion criteria:
(1) Orthopedic oder neurologic comorbility with relevant restricition of the agility or gait function 
(2) Cognitive impaitment which impacts everyday life (MMST<27)
(3) Severe depression or psicosis 
(4) Marked dyskinesia while being in medical ON-State
(5) Coronary heart disease with instable angina pectoris
(6) Kamptokormia > 20° or Pisasyndrom
(7) Episodes of gaitfreezing while walking normally in the past half-year
(8) More than one fall in the past 12 months
(9) Unilateral hearing loss > 40dB
(10) Balance problems in anamnesis or in one of the following tests, not caused by the IPS: Romberg-Test, Tandem gait, Pull-Test
(11) Rhythmic Auditive Stimulation or CuraSwing-Training in the past three months
